On December 5th, the third of the series of Inter-Club races between Ashcombe A.C., Thames Valley H. and ourselves, took place from the Ashcombe quarters. We won the team race in the usual easy fashion, whilst Arthur Allum led the field home, with Jack Flower as second man.
Right from the commencement of the run it was obvious that our boys were certain winners of the match, but the duel between Arthur Allum and Jack Flower for first place caused great interest.

A field of 32 faced the starter and Arthur Allum at once jumped to the front, accompanied by Jack Flower. These two ran right away from the rest of the field and Carter led a small bunch who were intent on the third place.

Jack Flower (15 yds.) jumped into his stride from the commencement and with about half a mile to go, took the lead ! Although not extended from this point, he recorded 9 min. 40 secs.—an excellent performance.

Jack Flower ran exceptionally well to finish where he did, but Bert Footer was, I think, a little disappointed at his own showing. It has long been one of Bert's ambitions to gain an English vest, and so we trust he will gain his reward next year.

It was with sadness that we received the recent news of JACK FLOWER's death at his home in Ruislip. Jack was one of our prominent runners in the 1930's and figures in many of our winning and placed teams as we climbed the ladder of fame.

ALBERT MACHER, JACK MACHER and JACK FLOWER were collectively in our thoughts during that minute of remembrance; and sharing that moment too was JACK HARTLEY of Coventry Godiva, guest at our last dinner in his capacity as ECCU President, and whose loss is mourned by the Midland club and its neighbours.
